title: A Fluorescent Intravital Imaging Approach to Study Load-Induced Calcium Signaling Dynamics in Mouse Osteocytes
protocol: Design and build the metatarsal loading device for use with an overhead multiphoton microscope.
Obtain commercially available actuator and load cell capable of accommodating loads up to 300 g.
Construct water bath, fulcrum pin, and loading bracket from titanium or stainless steel.
Calibrate strain magnitude values to the actuator displacement in advance for individual mouse groups.
Use mice with C57BL/6 background aged 16-18 weeks expressing fluorescent calcium indicator constructs in osteocytes.
Achieve osteocyte targeted expression by crossing flox-activated GCaMP6f and Dmp1-Cre mice.
Sterilize all surgical tools using an autoclave.
Load bracket, water bath, and fulcrum pin using an autoclave.
Disinfect microscope objectives with 100% ethanol.
Turn on the laser source.
Turn on the microscope.
Turn on the load cell.
Turn on the actuator.
Allow electronic components to warm up for 15-20 minutes prior to intravital imaging.
Connect and activate the actuator in the control device.
Connect and activate the load cell component in the control device.
Generate control software using Matlab, LabView, or Python based on user preference.
Prepare a sterile surgical stage.
Sterilize the surface with 70% ethanol.
Anesthetize the mouse with vaporized isoflurane mixed with medical-grade air or oxygen at a flowrate of 1 L/min.
Perform initial anesthetization in a rodent induction chamber with 3%-5% isoflurane.
Maintain anesthesia at 1%-2.5% isoflurane in a nose cone for surgical and intravital imaging procedures.
Monitor the mouse's body temperature with a rectal probe connected to a homeothermic-controlled heating pad positioned under the anesthetized animal.
Monitor the heart rate and oxygen saturation using a rodent pulse oximeter.
Keep the breath rate between 60-80 breaths per minute by adjusting the isoflurane dosage.
Place the mouse in a supine position.
Identify the location between the second and third metatarsals.
Make a scalpel incision through the dermis between the second and third metatarsals, starting at the distal end and progressing proximally along the length of the bones (~5 mm).
Using forceps, open the surgical site by pulling the skin toward the medial/lateral edges.
Resect the extensor tendons using straight Vannas scissors to expose the third metatarsal.
Insert the center fulcrum pin of the metatarsal loading device beneath the third metatarsal.
Move the pin proximally until it rests at the mid-shaft of the third metatarsal.
Ensure a direct interface between the bone and the pin, excluding any muscle and fascia.
Hold the ankle with forceps and place the foot into a DPBS filled water bath (8-10 mL).
Secure the paw in place with the loading bracket.
Connect the bracket to the actuator/load cell arrangement.
Very carefully pick up the loading device setup with the mouse and place it onto the microscope platform.
Start with a low magnification objective in epifluorescence mode to locate and center the mid-diaphysis of the bone.
After a region of interest is located, switch to a higher water immersion objective magnification (20x-40x).
Switch the optics to two-photon for detailed imaging.
Set the pixel density to 512 pixels x 512 pixels using Galvo/Resonance Area Control settings.
Reduce power in Power Control option to avoid photobleaching during ROI identification.
Increase PMT amplification in Galvo/Resonance Scanner Control settings for better signal detection.
Identify the surface of the bone in two-photon mode by looking for fibrous periosteum autofluorescence in the green channel using a bandpass filter centered at 525 nm.
Run a test loading bout to ensure surgical preparation stability within the loading device.
Switch on Servo and Move in Matlab code to perform loading.
Apply a small tare load.
Prepare haversine wave loading protocols ahead of time.
Input calibration parameters obtained in section 1.2 into the Matlab code.
Run the "Servo and Move" function from the Matlab code to perform loading.
Select a different region of interest along y- or z-directions if bone movement is visible during loading.
Adjust the surgical position of the pin manually underneath the third metatarsal if movement persists.
Conduct z-stack or t-series imaging according to the experimental design.
Set the excitation wavelength for the fluorescent indicator, such as 920 nm for GCaMP6f.
Use a resolution of 0.25-1 μm steps for z-stack imaging to capture features of osteocytes.
Sample at least 6x the loading rate for t-series imaging settings.
Image at 6 frames per second (FPS) for a 1 Hz loading rate in t-series imaging.
Collect non-loaded baseline data with each bout.
Perform 60 s of non-loaded imaging.
Follow with 60 s of loading and imaging.
Press Capture for data collection.
Wait at least 15 min between sequential loading bouts when collecting dynamic signaling data.
Do not leave the animal unattended until it has regained sufficient consciousness to maintain sternal recumbency.
